title: Staggered stability cadence and release digest - July 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft for a staggered stability cadence we want to try for the July 2026 launch. The goal is to reduce blast radius during initial ramp while giving product teams predictable capacity and clear go/no-go gates for each week.

Audience:
Release engineering, SRE, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, solutions-engineering, support on-call.

High-level plan (three-phase cadence):
1) Ramp (week 0-1) - small % of traffic to the new release, focus on correctness and basic latency SLOs.
2) Stabilize (week 2-3) - increase traffic, validate tail latency, refine autoscaling and batching heuristics.
3) Scale & Optimize (week 4-6) - full traffic, monitor cost-per-token and model-quality regressions, finalize release notes.

Weekly calendar (dates are illustrative, adapt to launch window):
- Week 0 (2026-07-12 to 2026-07-18): Canary + feature flag validation
  - Deploy canary to region-us-east-1 with 2 dedicated GPU nodes
  - Smoke tests (see preflight checklist) after canary deploy
  - Collect 48h of traces and error rates
  - Communication: #release-ops post with status and roll-out plan

- Week 1 (2026-07-19 to 2026-07-25): Micro-canary ramp to 5%
  - Gradual route weighting, monitor queue depth and KV-cache hit rate
  - Validate fallback model path under simulated GPU pressure
  - Ops dry run for rollback (execute rollback on staging to ensure scripts work)

- Week 2 (2026-07-26 to 2026-08-01): Mid-tier ramp to 25%
  - Load test new autoscale policy in a mirror environment
  - Start collecting quality-eval samples for generation regressions
  - Enable extended tracing for 30% of requests for 72h

- Week 3 (2026-08-02 to 2026-08-08): Stabilize at 50%
  - Run no-new-deploy freeze window for 48h during high traffic days
  - Validate billing and token accounting for routed requests
  - Finalize release notes draft and customer-facing breaking changes

- Week 4 (2026-08-09 to 2026-08-15): Full ramp readiness (internal only)
  - Canary regression check complete
  - SLOs green for 7 days (latency, error rate, cost/unit)
  - Communication: customer success briefing and documentation freeze

- Week 5-6 (2026-08-16 to 2026-08-29): Full launch and optimization
  - Route 100% traffic; monitor for 7-day stability window
  - Post-launch optimization (batch size tuning, cache TTL adjustments)
  - Create postmortem-lite template for early issues

Preflight checklist (must be green before any ramp):
- [ ] Release artifact built and checksum verified (artifact id: serving-runtime:v2026.7.2)
- [ ] Infra provisioning tested: capacity reserve for 120% of expected peak
- [ ] Smoke test suite (smoke/basic-gen/kv-cache) passes end-to-end in canary
- [ ] Canary alert channels configured and paged recipients validated
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards (latency p50/p95/p99, errors, token counts) present and baseline captured
- [ ] Rollback scripts reviewed and manual rollback performed once in staging
- [ ] Security scan (SCA), dependency checks completed and exceptions documented
- [ ] Release notes skeleton created and shared with product for sign-off

Release notes draft (to be edited into final customer-facing doc):
- Release name: Staggered Stability Release (internal: SSR-2026-07)
- Date: 2026-08-16 (target full launch)
- Highlights:
  - Improved batching heuristic that reduces per-token CPU by ~12% on long context paths (ENG-3421)
  - New fallback routing policy for out-of-region capacity loss (graceful downgrade path)
  - Telemetry: added token-level cost attribution per route for clearer unit economics
- Important notes for customers:
  - No breaking API changes expected. If you use pinned model versions, ensure you update rollout policy to allow fallback variants (see Migration Guidance below).
  - Known limitations: under extreme tail-latency conditions (p99 > 2.5s) the fallback may change model and slightly alter completions. We are monitoring and will publish more details in the KB.
- Migration guidance:
  - If you pin to model v1.4, add a config: allow_compatible_fallbacks=true to retain availability during region fallback scenarios.
  - For Dedicated customers: contact your solutions engineer to request a zero-downtime traffic migration window.

Rollback and mitigation matrix (summary):
- Symptom: sudden p99 spike (>3x baseline)
  - Immediate action: cut traffic to previous stable variant (route weight -> stable:100%), scale up error budgeting alerts, notify #oncall-sre
  - Post-action: collect traces + heap profiles, open JIRA:RELEASE-ROLLBACK-<timestamp>

- Symptom: increased model hallucination/regression (quality metric delta above threshold)
  - Immediate: activate QA-only canary and route test traffic, pause further ramp
  - Post-action: revert model weight to prior artifact; run evals to reproduce regression

Telemetry & SLO verification steps:
- Verify token accounting by comparing billing export to telemetry export for a 24h window
- Check p99 across all regions; if any region is > target, run region-isolation test
- Confirm KV cache hit ratio improved post-release (target: +8% vs baseline)

Communication templates (short):
- Slack status (post to #release-ops):
  - "[SSR-2026-07] Canary deployed to us-east-1. Smoke tests passing. Observability link: <dashboards>. Will start micro-ramp tomorrow 10:00 PT unless any blockers."

- Customer email (CS draft):
  - Subject: "Planned update to inference runtime (Aug 16) - what to expect"
  - Body: short bullets from Release notes; call to action if you pin models or need migration help.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm exact autoscaler buffer percentage required for Dedicated tenants under the new batching heuristic (action: ask infra team: Marcus)
- Need a short circuit to disable extended tracing automatically after X hours to avoid cost overruns (action: Aisha)
- Validate that fallback routing doesn't violate SLA terms for a small set of enterprise customers (legal/finance check)

Attachments & artifacts to add before finalizing:
- Full test matrix spreadsheet (link placeholder)
- Eval results for prompt-set-v7 (quality regression checks)
- Post-launch monitoring playbook (call tree + pager duties)

Appendix: short smoke test checklist (ordered):
1) Basic generation with 256 tokens, cold start latency < 800ms p50
2) Repeated KV-cache hits for a warm prefix (expect hit ratio > 70% for sequence of 10)
3) Forced model fallback scenario (simulate loss of one GPU node) and validate graceful response codes
4) Billing attribution: verify tokens show correct route label in billing export

Notes: keep this doc intentionally conversational. This is a working checklist and rollout calendar; treat as a living artifact. If you copy sections into Confluence or customer emails, please move the final content to the official launch notes template and get product sign-off.

Quick links (working):
- Staging dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference.internal/staging/ssr-2026-07
- Runbook template: https://confluence.redwood/cookbooks/release-runbook-template
- Oncall rota: https://roster.redwood/inference-sre

Last edits: 2026-07-22 - added stabilization week checklist and early rollback matrix.
